audits.title: ThTP5.10 A clinical audit of assessment of the risk of malnutrition and the subsequent nutritional support prescribed for older emergency laparotomy patients
audits.standard: NICE 2017: MUST on admission, with high-risk score triggering a response
audits.setting: Older emergency laparotomy patients on NELA database, Leeds Teaching Hospitals Trust

cycle1.result: 99.3% had MUST recorded on admission; of 114 high MUST patients, 35% had no dietetic review and 24% received neither oral nor parenteral supplementation.

audits.other_findings: 30-day mortality 13.9%; a supplementation protocol before dietetic review and prescriber education are recommended.
audits.citation: Windle A, Burke D, Ispoglou T, Nair S. ThTP5.10 A clinical audit of assessment of the risk of malnutrition and the subsequent nutritional support prescribed for older emergency laparotomy patients. British Journal of Surgery. 2023;110(Supplement_6). doi:10.1093/bjs/znad241.293.

audits.title: Assessment for the risk of malnutrition and nutritional support in older emergency laparotomy patients: a clinical audit
audits.standard: NICE 2017: MUST on admission and nutritional support for high-risk (MUST 2 or above) patients
audits.setting: Single NHS trust, NELA patients aged 65 or over (Leeds Teaching Hospitals affiliation)

cycle1.result: 98% had a MUST score; of 114 high-risk patients, 35% had no dietetic review and 24% received no oral or parenteral supplementation.

audits.other_findings: Nutritional screening is not currently included in NELA.
audits.citation: Windle A, Nair S, Ispoglou T, Burke D. Assessment for the risk of malnutrition and nutritional support in older emergency laparotomy patients: a clinical audit. British Journal of Surgery. 2023;110(Supplement_10). doi:10.1093/bjs/znad388.009.

audits.title: WP8.3 - "Effectiveness of Malnutrition Screen and Interventions for Surgical Inpatients - A MUST Score Based Audit"
audits.standard: Malnutrition Universal Screening Tool (MUST) completion, accuracy and updating

cycle1.result: MUST scores completed in 83.3% but with significant inaccuracies (BMI, weight loss, acute disease effect); only 15.6% updated.

audits.intervention: Malnutrition awareness week with dietitians and teaching sessions for healthcare staff on the MUST tool.
audits.other_findings: Staff training gaps and inconsistent scoring were noted, though clinical teams identified at-risk patients by judgement and started interventions promptly.
audits.citation: Ylli K, Sheehan C, Nugent T. WP8.3 - "Effectiveness of Malnutrition Screen and Interventions for Surgical Inpatients - A MUST Score Based Audit". British Journal of Surgery. 2024;111(Supplement_8). doi:10.1093/bjs/znae197.214.

audits.title: Nutritional screening among patients with cancer in an acute care hospital: a best practice implementation project.
audits.standard: Three JBI criteria for nutritional screening

cycle1.result: Validated tool used 100%; screening on admission 96%; action plan for at-risk patients 46%.

audits.title: Nutritional assessment in elderly care: a MUST!
audits.standard: Malnutrition Universal Screening Tool (MUST) documented, correctly calculated and acted on
audits.setting: Elderly care ward, Watford General Hospital, West Hertfordshire Hospitals NHS Trust

cycle1.result: MUST scores calculated in 73%; dietitian referral 62%

audits.intervention: Liaison with hospital teams, encouraging regular nurse training, and weekly dietitian ward rounds to screen for malnutrition

cycle2.result: MUST scores calculated in 97%; dietitian referral 86% (second cycle)

audits.other_findings: Three cycles (May, July, November 2013; n=64, 62, 63); MUST scores were often miscalculated owing to BMI errors and unknown previous weights.
audits.citation: Frank M, Sivagnanaratnam A, Bernstein J. Nutritional assessment in elderly care: a MUST!. BMJ Qual Improv Rep. 2015;4(1):u204810.w2031. doi:10.1136/bmjquality.u204810.w2031. PMID: 26734346.

audits.title: Research identified variation in nutrition practice by community prescribing dietitians with regards to the identification and management of malnutrition amongst community dwelling adults.
audits.standard: NICE CG32 standards 1.3.1 (indications for nutrition support) and 1.5.6 (monitoring); target 100% compliance

cycle1.result: Compliance with standard 1.3.1 was 46% and with standard 1.5.6 82%.

audits.other_findings: 86% (n = 13) of patients reported satisfaction (target 90%); nationally 89% of dietitians used weight and 87% BMI as outcomes.

audits.title: Improving nutritional assessment in acute medical admissions at a district general hospital.
audits.standard: Completed accurate MUST within 6 hours of AMU arrival (80%); dietitian referral within 48 hours for MUST ≥2 (100%)
audits.setting: Acute Medical Unit, Queen Elizabeth Hospital King's Lynn, district general hospital

cycle1.result: MUST correct in 111/150 (74%); 1/9 (11%) high-risk patients referred to dietitians

audits.intervention: Face-to-face training, e-learning module in induction and ward MUST troubleshooting booklets

cycle2.result: MUST correct in 77/101 (76%); 2/4 (50%) high-risk patients referred

audits.other_findings: Nurses (n = 19) felt confident but averaged 67% on an objective assessment; targets not met.
audits.citation: Wong JJ, Tailor BV, Chen F, Florance R. Improving nutritional assessment in acute medical admissions at a district general hospital. Int J Risk Saf Med. 2022;33(S1):S57-S61. doi:10.3233/jrs-227025. PMID: 35871369.

audits.title: Are We Identifying Malnutrition in Hospitalized Patients with Hematologic Malignancies? Results from a Quality Clinical Audit.
audits.standard: Malnutrition Universal Screening Tool (MUST) screening within 48 h of admission with nutritional support as indicated
audits.setting: Two haematology units, Laikon General Hospital, Athens; tertiary university hospital

cycle1.result: 37.3% at high risk of malnutrition on admission; only 5 patients (2.7%) received nutritional support as indicated.

audits.other_findings: 26.5% reported reduced food intake in the past 5 days; low awareness of malnutrition among the medical team.
audits.citation: Kanioura E, Tzanninis IG, Poulia KA, Stamou A, Liaskas A, Politis D, et al.. Are We Identifying Malnutrition in Hospitalized Patients with Hematologic Malignancies? Results from a Quality Clinical Audit. Diseases. 2022;10(3):40. doi:10.3390/diseases10030040. PMID: 35892734.

audits.title: Documentation of anthropometrics in people with cancer: a cross-site collaboration audit in four hospital settings in the UK.
audits.standard: Complete and accurate documentation of anthropometric measurements, MUST screening and dietetic referral
audits.setting: Four day-treatment units for systemic anti-cancer treatment in England

cycle1.result: Weight documented in 58-85% and height in 94-98%; BMI documented on day of treatment in 55% on average (range 7-85%); MUST completed in ≤3% in each centre.

audits.other_findings: Dietetic referral practices varied between centres; 100 patients per unit.
audits.citation: Tabacchi F, Oberai R, Parmar K, Oxley L, Coe S, Iatridi V, et al.. Documentation of anthropometrics in people with cancer: a cross-site collaboration audit in four hospital settings in the UK. Support Care Cancer. 2024;32(11):720. doi:10.1007/s00520-024-08931-3. PMID: 39387942.

audits.title: Improving the performance of nutrition screening through a series of quality improvement initiatives.
audits.standard: Correct completion of 3-Minute Nutrition Screening tool and referral of at-risk patients to dietetics

cycle1.result: Screening error rate 33%; 5% blank or missing forms; 10% of at-risk patients not referred; referral took up to 7.5 days

audits.intervention: Screening protocol, training, nurse-initiated online dietetic referral, closed-loop feedback and removal of the most error-prone tool component

cycle2.result: Non-referrals 3%; mean screening to referral time 0.3 ± 0.4 days (from 4.3 ± 1.8)

audits.other_findings: Annual audits 2008-2013 on 4,467 patients in total; 2009 error rate 31%, non-referrals 7% (2010) and 4% (2011).
audits.citation: Lim SL, Ng SC, Lye J, Loke WC, Ferguson M, Daniels L. Improving the performance of nutrition screening through a series of quality improvement initiatives. Jt Comm J Qual Patient Saf. 2014;40(4):178-186. doi:10.1016/s1553-7250(14)40023-0. PMID: 24864526.
